extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for the NIH Pathway to Independence (K99/R00) award (NIA example)
extracted.subtask_description: A sample K99/R00 (NIH Pathway to Independence) application showing the sections, content, experimental rigor, career development plan, mentor commitments, and contingency planning expected for a competitive postdoctoral-to-independent-investigator award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required PHS/424/PHS398 components (Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include all standard SF424 R&R and PHS-398 components listed in the Table of Contents (e.g., SF 424 R&R Cover Page; Project Summary/Abstract; Project Narrative; Bibliography & References Cited; Facilities & Other Resources; Equipment; Senior/Key Person; Research & Related Budget; PHS398 Cover Page Supplement; PHS 398 Career Development Award; Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development; Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research; Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentor(s); Letters of Support; Description of Institutional Environment; Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development; PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information; Resource Sharing; Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TOC provides the exact components reviewers expect; include each section in the application and follow PHS/NIH instructions for each form/section. The sample's TOC shows exact ordering and section titles to mirror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with FOA-specific requirements (Clinical trial policy, FOA number/title)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must follow the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) terms; e.g., FOA: PA19-130, FOA Title: NIH Pathway to Independence Award (Parent K99/R00 - Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed), Clinical Trial: Not Allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether the FOA allows clinical trials; adhere to FOA constraints (if Clinical Trial Not Allowed, do not propose a clinical trial). Include FOA identifiers on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract communicates significance and approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary should concisely state the scientific problem, the gap in knowledge, hypotheses, the approach (two-phase K99 then R00), and the expected outcomes and impact (example: cytoskeletal decline in aging, tools developed for in vivo imaging, multipronged screening approach, and proposed aims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Project Summary to set context (what is known/unknown), highlight preliminary tools/techniques, describe the multi-pronged strategy and the high-level aims, and explain how the work advances the field and the candidate's transition to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative communicates relevance to public health
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Narrative should briefly explain why the project matters for health/aging and the broader implications (example text: link between actin cytoskeleton decline and aging-related cellular dysfunction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it non-technical and focused on public-health significance (for lay readers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Background: demonstrate productivity and relevant expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate background should provide evidence of scientific productivity (e.g., first-author publications, novel methods developed), breadth of technical expertise, and prior accomplishments (example: seven first-author publications, methods for multi-color live-cell imaging), plus evidence of leadership and resourcefulness (e.g., management experience, time management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize publications, unique techniques created, independent projects, and any rapid progress (e.g., PhD in four years with 4.0 GPA) as evidence of readiness for independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Background: teaching, mentoring, and diversity engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe teaching and mentoring experiences across educational levels and engagement in programs to increase under-represented minorities in STEM (example: teaching at Columbia and Hunter College, involvement with NIH Bridges to Baccalaureate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete roles and outcomes (courses taught, mentoring numbers, program involvement) to support ability to run a research group and commitment to training and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Goals and Objectives: clear short-term and long-term plan
rubrics_metrics.description: State short-term goals (complete postdoc training, acquire new skills like data science) and long-term goals (establish independent research group, research focus expansion), and explain how the K99/R00 will enable these transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about skill gaps to be addressed and how training will bridge to an independent PI role; connect activities to future faculty responsibilities (research, teaching, mentorship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from Mentor: document intellectual and resource independence plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the candidate's research differs from the mentor's lab interests, how overlap will be avoided, and assurances about access to reagents and intellectual ownership (example: mentor maintains open communication and allows trainee to take reagents; candidate's cytoskeletal focus is distinct from mentor's primary research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear language and (ideally) mentor statements confirming independence and resource access; describe plans to prevent scientific overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Career Development/Training Activities: concrete training roadmap
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed plan of training activities (technical and professional) during the award period, including specific courses, hands-on collaborations, tutorials, mentoring relationships, advisory committee meetings (frequency), and timelines (example: mass spectrometry training, bioinformatics training with named collaborators, committee meetings every 6–9 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific skills to be acquired, named mentors/experts and their roles, concrete courses/tools (e.g., 'Databases and tools of Bioinformatics' at UC Berkeley), and scheduled interactions to demonstrate feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor and Advisory Committee: describe roles & letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify mentor(s) and outside experts with explicit roles (e.g., transcription expert, cytoskeleton expert, proximity-labeling expert) and include letters of support confirming mentoring commitments and specific training contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify each mentor's contributions to training and science, and attach strong letters of support that detail resources, training, and access to expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: testable hypotheses and focused objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Each aim should state the hypothesis, the rationale, and a clear experimental approach (example Aims 1–3: characterize molecular pathways, test non-autonomous signaling, and map molecular interactors via proximity labeling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep aims concise, logically ordered, and feasible within the award period; include sub-aims and experimental endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy: multi-pronged approaches and use of preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a detailed research strategy that integrates multiple complementary methods (e.g., live-cell imaging, synthetic lethality screening, transcriptomics, whole-genome CRISPR screening) and leverages preliminary data and tools developed by the candidate (example: LifeAct-mRuby imaging system, prior screens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how different approaches cross-validate findings and justify methodological choices with preliminary results where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of experimental design: blinding, randomization, replicates, and multiple approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: All qualitative measurements will be double-blinded (e.g., lifespans and microscopy). All animals and samples will be assigned at random. Provide all replicates and sample sizes. Use multiple independent approaches to address each question to avoid method-specific bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state blinding/randomization procedures, statistical planned sample sizes, number of biological/technical replicates, and complementary methods to strengthen inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls and specificity: design of negative/positive and specificity controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate controls to subtract background and validate specificity (example: cytoplasmic mRuby::miniTurbo without LifeAct to remove cytoplasmic proteins; probe pulldowns with anti-actin antibodies as positive control; positive perturbation controls such as tropomyosin knockdown, arp-2/3 inhibition, or actin knockdown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and describe both technical and biological controls, and plan validation assays to confirm target enrichment and specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and spatial experimental control
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spatial promoters and temporal control systems (example: tissue-specific promoters and a degron/auxin system to control LifeAct-miniTurbo expression and allow temporal resolution of labeling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how temporal induction/repression and tissue specificity will be achieved and validated; include timing for induction/collection (example: remove auxin 24 hours prior to collection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection design across tissues and aging timepoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect samples across defined tissues and ages with planned timepoints reflecting 'young' and 'old' (example: muscle and intestine D1 and D10; hypodermis D3 and D7) and include perturbation timepoints as controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify chosen timepoints based on prior characterization and ensure sufficient biological replicates for each tissue/time combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proteomics & data analysis plan and core-facility collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe proteomic workflow (e.g., purify biotinylated proteins, TMT labeling, MS/MS analysis), planned software/tools (X! Tandem, Scaffold Q, SafeQuant), and named collaborations with mass-spec cores and experts (example: Brett Phinney at UC Davis; Ting lab for analysis guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete analysis pipelines, collaborators' roles, and plan for data processing, normalization, and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization and validation of screening hits
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to prioritize candidates (e.g., genes with known actin regulatory functions that differ across tissues) for functional validation via RNAi knockdown and tissue-specific overexpression and to assess effects on cytoskeletal health and longevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicit, reproducible criteria for selecting hits for follow-up and the assays that will be used for validation and functional testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency (Caveat) planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide alternative approaches if primary strategy fails (example caveat: expand analysis to all proteins identified in mass-spec if no known actin regulators show tissue specificity; perform large-scale RNAi screens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include feasible fallback plans, resources available to implement them, and criteria for when to switch to contingency approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and allocation of aims to K99 versus R00 phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a timeline mapping specific aims and milestones to K99 Year 1/2 and R00 Year 1–3, indicating when experiments, method development, and validations will occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear table/Gantt mapping aims to years to show feasibility and appropriate pacing for transitioning to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics/compliance reporting (Animals/Humans/Clinical Trial status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the presence/absence of vertebrate animals, human subjects, and clinical trial involvement (example fields: Animals: N; Humans: N; Clinical Trial: N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurately declare compliance needs and include required human/animal protocol approvals or plans if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and justification per year
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Research & Related Budget details and a Budget Justification (example shows Subtotal Direct Costs per year: Year1–5 values listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per-year direct costs, justifications for major cost categories (personnel, supplies, core fees), and ensure alignment with FOA/NIH limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited: thorough citation of relevant literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a comprehensive references list supporting background, preliminary data, methods, and interpretation (sample contains many domain-specific citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite key foundational and recent work to justify hypotheses and methods; ensure citations are complete and formatted per instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Include plans for authentication of critical reagents (example: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources section listed in TOC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how cell lines, antibodies, strains, and key reagents will be authenticated and tracked to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a training plan for RCR as required for career development awards (section listed in TOC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail RCR topics to be covered, format (courses, seminars), timing, and who will provide training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Letters of Support that document collaborators' commitments, scope of contributions, access to facilities, and roles in training/analysis (TOC item and examples throughout narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure letters are specific about resources, time commitments, and what the collaborator will practically deliver (e.g., training, access to core facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Institutional Environment and Institutional Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the institutional environment and explicit institutional commitment to the candidate's career development and research (TOC items: Description of Institutional Environment; Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should state commitments such as protected research time, start-up resources, space, and access to cores; include letters documenting institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sample/application text as permissible educational example (copyright notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sample application includes a copyright notice: awardee allows use of material for nonprofit educational purposes if unchanged and credited (PI, awardee organization, and NIH NIA must be credited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reusing text/figures from sample applications, follow the stated permission terms—keep material unchanged and credit sources.
